
# Enviromentypes

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# 0. Libraries
library(sf)
library(terra)   
library(exactextractr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

library(purrr)
```

## Landcover percentage
**Generate Bufferzones**
```{r extract-buffer, eval = FALSE}
## — 0. Load sample points and buffers —
sample_points <- read.csv(
  "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/sample_points.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
points_sf   <- st_as_sf(sample_points,
                        coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                        crs    = 4326)
points_proj     <- st_transform(points_sf, 28355)

# — 1. Build virtual mosaic & reproject —
tile_files   <- list.files(
  "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/Landcover/Tif",
  pattern    = "\\.tif$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
rasters      <- lapply(tile_files, terra::rast)
mosaic_all   <- do.call(mosaic, c(rasters, list(fun = "first")))
lc_proj      <- project(mosaic_all, "EPSG:28355")

buffers   <- st_buffer(points_proj, dist = 150)
extracted <- exact_extract(lc_proj, buffers)
```

```{r style, eval = false   }

summary_list <- lapply(seq_along(extracted), function(i) {
  df  <- extracted[[i]]
  agg <- aggregate(df$coverage_fraction,
                   by   = list(class = round(df$value)),
                   FUN  = sum)
  colnames(agg) <- c("land_cover_class", "fraction")
  agg$percent <- round(100 * agg$fraction / sum(agg$fraction), 2)
  agg$id      <- sample_points$id[i]
  agg
})
result_df <- bind_rows(summary_list)

# 1) Read & strip ns
qml_path <- "C:/Users/Lukas/Documents/GitHub/btp_metagenomics/Landcover/landcover_class_cyear_4_style.qml"
qml  <- xml_ns_strip(read_xml(qml_path))

# 2) Grab the palette entries
entries <- xml_find_all(qml, ".//paletteEntry")
stopifnot(length(entries) > 0)  # confirm you actually found some

# 3) Build your style table from those entries
style_df <- tibble(
  land_cover_class       = as.integer(xml_attr(entries, "value")),
  land_cover_label       = xml_attr(entries, "label"),
  color                  = xml_attr(entries, "color")
) %>%
  mutate(
    form = case_when(
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Cultivated Terrestrial Vegetated: Herbaceous")    ~ "Cultivated Herbaceous
      ",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Cultivated Terrestrial Vegetated: Woody")    ~ "Cultivated woody",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Natural Terrestrial Vegetated: Woody")     ~ "Natural - Woody",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Natural Terrestrial Vegetated: Herbaceous")~ "Natural - Herbaceous",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Aquatic Vegetated")                        ~ "Aquatic",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Natural Surface")                          ~ "Bare Surface",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Artificial Surface")                       ~ "Urban/Artificial",
      TRUE                                                                      ~ NA_character_
    ),
    density = case_when(
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Closed \\(greater than 65") ~ 80,
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Open \\(40 to 65")         ~ 52.5,
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Open \\(15 to 40")         ~ 27.5,
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Sparse \\(4 to 15")        ~ 9.5,
      TRUE                                                     ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(land_cover_class, form, density, everything())

```

```{r pivot }

# 1. Join in the density & labels
result_df <- result_df %>%
  left_join(
    style_df %>% select(land_cover_class, density, land_cover_label),
    by = "land_cover_class"
  )

# 2. Drop rows that can’t be assigned a class or label
result_df_clean <- result_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(land_cover_class), !is.na(land_cover_label))

# 3. Compute class‐mean densities and impute missing
class_means <- result_df_clean %>%
  group_by(land_cover_label) %>%
  summarize(mean_veg_density = mean(density, na.rm = TRUE))

result_df_imputed <- result_df_clean %>%
  left_join(class_means, by = "land_cover_label") %>%
  mutate(
    # if density is already there, keep it; otherwise use the class mean
    density = coalesce(density, mean_veg_density)
  ) %>%
  select(-mean_veg_density)  # drop the helper column

# 4. Pivot, fill, and summarize
landcover_wide <- result_df_imputed %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = id,
    names_from  = land_cover_label,
    values_from = c(percent, density),
    values_fill = list(percent = 0, density = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Cultivated_Total = rowSums(
      select(., starts_with("percent_Cultivated Terrestrial")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Native_Total     = rowSums(
      select(
        .,
        starts_with("percent_Natural Terrestrial"),
        starts_with("percent_Natural Aquatic Vegetated")
      ),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Water            = rowSums(
      select(., starts_with("percent_Water:")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    # split your former Artificial_Bare into two pieces:
    Bare_Surface      = rowSums(
      select(., starts_with("percent_Natural Surface:")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Urban_Artificial  = rowSums(
      select(., starts_with("percent_Artificial Surface:")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Overall_Density = sum(
      c_across(starts_with("percent_")) / 100 *
      c_across(starts_with("density_")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r barplot visualisation data, eval = FALSE}

# 1) Define your exact colors
group_colors <- c(
  "Cultivated Vegetation - Woody"      = "#6a51a3",
  "Cultivated Vegetation - Herbaceous" = "#9e9ac8",
  "Natural Vegetation - Woody"         = "#006400",
  "Natural Vegetation - Herbaceous"    = "#1b9e77",
  "Natural Vegetation - General"       = "#b2df8a",
  "Aquatic Vegetation"                 = "#41b6c4",
  "Bare Surface"                       = "#e6ab02",
  "Urban/Artificial"                   = "#757575",
  "Other"                              = "#cccccc"
)

# 2) Start from your long, imputed data
long_df <- result_df_imputed %>%
  select(id, land_cover_label, percent)

# 3) Bucket into exactly the groups you want
long_df <- long_df %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Cultivated Terrestrial Vegetated: Woody")      ~ "Cultivated Vegetation - Woody",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Cultivated Terrestrial Vegetated: Herbaceous") ~ "Cultivated Vegetation - Herbaceous",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Natural Terrestrial Vegetated: Woody")         ~ "Natural Vegetation - Woody",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Natural Terrestrial Vegetated: Herbaceous")    ~ "Natural Vegetation - Herbaceous",
      # anything else “Natural Terrestrial Vegetated” → general
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Natural Terrestrial Vegetated:")               ~ "Natural Vegetation - General",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Aquatic Vegetated")                             ~ "Aquatic Vegetation",
      # Sparse/Scattered or bare surface labels
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "Scattered|Sparse|Natural Surface:")             ~ "Bare Surface",
      str_detect(land_cover_label, "^Artificial Surface:")                          ~ "Urban/Artificial",
      TRUE                                                                          ~ "Other"
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = names(group_colors))
  )

# 4) Drop NAs & Water, sum by id×group, then re-scale so each id sums to 100%
plot_df <- long_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(land_cover_label), group != "Water") %>%
  group_by(id, group) %>%
summarise(pct = sum(percent, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
group_by(id) %>%
mutate(pct = pct / sum(pct) * 100) %>%
ungroup()

# 5) Plot
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = factor(id), y = pct, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Landcover Breakdown per Sample (No Water, Normalized)",
    x     = "Sample ID",
    y     = "Percent Cover",
    fill  = "Category"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

plot_df_wide <- plot_df %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = pct)
```

```{r climate variable data, eval = FALSE}

# 5a. Grab the Australia bioclim variables (returns a SpatRaster)
wc_aus <- worldclim_country(
  country = "AUS",    # ISO code
  var     = "bio",    # all 19 BIO variables
  res     = 0.5,      # 30″ resolution
  path    = "data/aus"
)

# 5b. Rename the layers to "bio1"…"bio19" so we can index 1–12
orig <- names(wc_aus)
new  <- sub(".*bio[_~\\.](\\d+)$", "bio\\1", orig)
names(wc_aus) <- new

# 5c. Reproject your 150 m buffers into geographic coords (lon/lat)
buffers_ll <- st_transform(buffers, st_crs(wc_aus))

# 5d. Extract weighted means for bio1…bio12 and give them proper names ----

# a) Define the codes and descriptive names
bio_codes <- paste0("bio", 1:12)
bio_names <- c(
  annual_mean_temp           = "bio1",
  mean_diurnal_range         = "bio2",
  isothermality              = "bio3",
  temp_seasonality           = "bio4",
  max_temp_warmest_month     = "bio5",
  min_temp_coldest_month     = "bio6",
  temp_annual_range          = "bio7",
  mean_temp_wettest_quarter  = "bio8",
  mean_temp_driest_quarter   = "bio9",
  mean_temp_warmest_quarter  = "bio10",
  mean_temp_coldest_quarter  = "bio11",
  annual_precipitation       = "bio12"
)

# b) Pull out each layer’s weighted mean into a list
means_list <- purrr::map(bio_codes, function(code) {
  exactextractr::exact_extract(
    wc_aus[[code]],
    buffers_ll,
    fun = function(vals, coverage_fraction) {
      weighted.mean(vals, coverage_fraction, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  )
})

# c) Build a tibble: sample IDs + one column per bio
clim_df <- tibble::tibble(id = sample_points$id) %>%
  dplyr::bind_cols(as_tibble(purrr::set_names(means_list, bio_codes))) %>%
  # d) Rename from bio# → descriptive
  dplyr::rename(!!!bio_names)

print(clim_df)

```

```{r population variable data, eval = FALSE}
# 1. Download & load the 1 km WorldPop density for Australia -------------
out1km <- "data/pop1km/aus_pd_2020_1km.tif"
dir.create(dirname(out1km), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

download.file(
  "https://data.worldpop.org/GIS/Population_Density/Global_2000_2020_1km/2020/AUS/aus_pd_2020_1km.tif",
  out1km, mode = "wb"
)
pop1km_rast <- rast(out1km)

# 2. Reproject your 150 m buffers into the raster’s CRS (WGS84 lon/lat)
buffers_ll <- st_transform(buffers, st_crs(pop1km_rast))

# 3. For each buffer, compute the mean density (people / km²)
pop1km_mean <- exact_extract(pop1km_rast, buffers_ll, fun = "mean")

# 4. Assemble into a data‐frame
pop1km_df <- tibble(
  id              = sample_points$id,
  pop_density_1km = pop1km_mean
)

print(pop1km_df)
```


**finegrade vs broad enviroment diversity**
```{r landcover_proportion matrix}
# 1) Build proportions from landcover_wide
landcover_prop <- landcover_wide %>%
  select(id, starts_with("percent_")) %>%
  mutate(across(-id, ~ . / 100))

prop_matrix <- landcover_prop %>%
  select(-id) %>%
  as.matrix()

prop_matrix[is.na(prop_matrix)] <- 0

# 2) Compute Hill numbers
h0 <- rowSums(prop_matrix > 0)
H  <- -rowSums(ifelse(prop_matrix > 0, prop_matrix * log(prop_matrix), 0))
h1 <- exp(H)
h2 <- 1 / rowSums(prop_matrix^2)

# 3) Bind back to the matching ids
hill_df_full <- data.frame(
  id = landcover_prop$id,
  h0 = h0,
  h1 = h1,
  h2 = h2
)

broad_prop <- plot_df_wide %>%
  mutate(across(-id, ~ . / 100))    # convert % → proportions

broad_mat <- broad_prop %>%
  select(-id) %>%
  as.matrix()
broad_mat[is.na(broad_mat)] <- 0    # just in case

# 2) Function to compute Hill numbers
compute_hills <- function(mat) {
  h0 <- rowSums(mat > 0)
  H1 <- -rowSums(ifelse(mat > 0, mat * log(mat), 0), na.rm = TRUE)
  h1 <- exp(H1)
  h2 <- 1 / rowSums(mat^2)
  tibble(h0 = h0, h1 = h1, h2 = h2)
}

# 3) Compute broad‐scale hills
hills_broad <- compute_hills(broad_mat)

# 4) Assemble into a data.frame with IDs
hill_broad_df <- tibble(
  id      = broad_prop$id,
  h0_broad = hills_broad$h0,
  h1_broad = hills_broad$h1,
  h2_broad = hills_broad$h2
)

# 5) Combine with your existing fine‐scale hills
hill_compare <- hill_df_full %>%
  left_join(hill_broad_df, by = "id")

# 6) Inspect & correlate
print(hill_compare)

# correlation between fine‐ and broad‐scale diversities
cor_mat <- hill_compare %>%
  select(h0, h0_broad, h1, h1_broad, h2, h2_broad) %>%
  cor()
print(cor_mat)

# 1) Numerical correlations with significance
tests <- list(
  h0  = cor.test(hill_compare$h0,  hill_compare$h0_broad),
  h1  = cor.test(hill_compare$h1,  hill_compare$h1_broad),
  h2  = cor.test(hill_compare$h2,  hill_compare$h2_broad)
)

# extract the r and p‐value neatly
corr_stats <- tibble(
  order    = c("h0","h1","h2"),
  r        = c(tests$h0$estimate,
               tests$h1$estimate,
               tests$h2$estimate),
  p_value  = c(tests$h0$p.value,
               tests$h1$p.value,
               tests$h2$p.value)
)
print(corr_stats)


# Inspect
print(hill_df_full)
```

**hill visualisation**
```{r hill_visualisation}

# 1) Compute a distance matrix on the 3 Hill numbers
hill_mat <- hill_df_full %>% select(h0, h1, h2) %>% as.matrix()
d       <- dist(hill_mat)          # Euclidean by default

# 2) Hierarchical clustering
hc      <- hclust(d, method = "ward.D2")

# 3) Cut the tree into k clusters (change k to taste)
k       <- 4
clusters <- cutree(hc, k = k)

# 4) Attach cluster labels
hill_df_cl <- hill_df_full %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(clusters))

# 5) Plot colored by cluster
ggplot(hill_df_cl %>% pivot_longer(h0:h2, names_to="q", values_to="value"),
       aes(x=q, y=value, group=id, color=cluster)) +
  geom_line(alpha=0.6) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Hill Curves, clustered into", k, "groups"),
    x     = "Hill order (q)",
    y     = "Effective diversity",
    color = "Cluster"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot(hc, labels = hill_df_full$id, main = "Dendrogram of Samples by Hill Numbers")
rect.hclust(hc, k = k, border = 2:5)  # draws boxes around your k clusters


```

```{r dominante_landcover}
# Pivot to long for easier processing
dominant_by_sample <- plot_df_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -id,
    names_to  = "dominant_landcover",
    values_to = "dom_percent_cover"
  ) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  filter(dom_percent_cover == max(dom_percent_cover, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%   # in case of ties, pick the first
  ungroup()

# 3) Join it back onto plot_df_wide

  left_join(dominant_by_sample, by = "id")
```

```{r dominant_boxplot}

# 1) Compute fine-scale Shannon H per sample
fine_shannon_df <- landcover_wide %>%
  # convert % → proportions
  select(id, starts_with("percent_")) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("percent_"), ~ . / 100)) %>%
  # compute H = –∑ p * log(p)
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    shannon = -sum(
      c_across(starts_with("percent_")) * 
      log(c_across(starts_with("percent_"))),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(id, shannon)

# 2) Bring in each sample’s dominant landcover (from your broad table)
shannon_by_dominant <- fine_shannon_df %>%
  left_join(
    plot_df_wide %>% select(id, dominant_landcover),
    by = "id"
  )

# 3) Plot fine-scale Shannon by dominant landcover
ggplot(shannon_by_dominant, 
       aes(x = dominant_landcover, y = shannon, fill = dominant_landcover)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = .8, outlier.color = "red", outlier.size = 1.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Fine-scale Shannon Diversity by Dominant Landcover",
    x     = "Dominant Landcover",
    y     = "Shannon Diversity (H)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

```
